ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A closed cylinder is connected to both ends of a U-shaped tube, and the cylinder wall is thermally conductive. The U-shaped tube contains a liquid with a density of $\rho{=}7.5{\times}10^{2}\mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^{3}$. A piston divides the cylinder into left and right gas chambers. Initially, the volume of the left gas chamber is half that of the right gas chamber, and the gas pressure in both chambers is $p_{0}{=}4.5{\times}10^{3}\mathrm{Pa}$. The external temperature remains constant. When the piston is slowly pulled to the right until the volumes of the left and right gas chambers are equal, what is the height difference $h$ of the liquid levels in the U-shaped tube? Take the gravitational acceleration as $g{=}10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, and neglect the volume of the gas in the U-shaped tube and the volume of the piston rod.

1. When the piston is slowly pulled to the right until the volumes of the gas on both sides are equal, what is the height difference $h$ between the liquid levels on both sides of the U-tube?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a horizontally placed closed cylinder, whose interior is divided by a piston with diagonal-line shading into left and right two gas chambers; the piston rod extends to the right. The left and right ends of the cylinder are respectively connected to the U-shaped tube below, and there is dark liquid in the bottom of the U-shaped tube and in the vertical sections on both sides, so when the pressures of the left and right gas chambers are different, it will cause a liquid-level height difference. Then reason: Let the initial volume of the left gas chamber be V, then the initial volume of the right gas chamber is 2V, and the total gas volume is 3V. Finally the volumes of the left and right gas chambers are equal, so each is 3V/2. Since the cylinder wall conducts heat and the external temperature is constant, the slow process can be regarded as the left and right gases respectively undergoing isothermal changes, satisfying Boyle's law. Left side: p_L·(3V/2)=p0·V, so p_L=(2/3)p0. Right side: p_R·(3V/2)=p0·2V, so p_R=(4/3)p0. Therefore the pressure difference between the two sides is Δp=p_R-p_L=(2/3)p0=(2/3)×4.5×10^3 Pa=3.0×10^3 Pa. The liquid column equilibrium in the U-shaped tube satisfies Δp=ρgh, so h=Δp/(ρg)=3000/(7.5×10^2×10)=0.40 m=40 cm.
